summary: Round 3, production pass on a prose-only split (backlog rows + ADR-0043 + two comment pointers). ALL FOUR ROUND-2 FINDINGS LANDED, AND EACH ONE LANDED AT EVERY SITE ITS CLAIM APPEARS, which is the check this family keeps failing. F1: the escape is gone from M5.45g criterion 6 -- the row now reads 'THE PRODUCTION IMPLEMENTATION DOES NOT SHIP HERE, FULL STOP' and records the rejected clause and why (it contradicted M5.45f's cell and only postponed the ~400 GETs); grep for 'behind a flag' finds it in no other row, and M5.45f's cell carries the identical absolute form, so the two rows now agree. F2: M5.45e's prose and State cell both say M5.45g. F3: ADR-0043:96 now names M5.39 (historical), M5.45d (hub) and M5.45h (consumer), which is the correct decomposition of that sentence -- the hub mint is what a per-run range grant would defeat. F4: the 'DECLINED' claim is retracted at BOTH sites -- :109-116 under Decision (b) and :209-215 in the Status note -- with the honest narrower statement ('no range is EXPRESSIBLE today') in both, and M5.45f named as the owner in both. THE OVERRIDE'S THIRD CONDITION IS TRUE AGAINST THE DIFF: `git diff --cached` touches exactly two `src/main` files, Delivery.java:17-18 and SubscriptionHub.java:449-450, and both hunks are comment text changing a row id -- no statement, no signature, no annotation, no import. (The SubscriptionHub hunk is a `//` comment inside `publishSegment`, not javadoc as the override line says; the substance of the condition -- no production logic -- holds exactly.) COST LENS: the split is now closed against the rate it was splitting away from. M5.45f is ADR-only; M5.45g ships a test fetcher and criterion 6 forbids a production one; M5.45h owns the coalescing at the right unit (one fetch per (node, segment), flat in nodes and segments, asserted at K=64 runs on ONE node against a fake counting INVOCATIONS rather than distinct urls). I walked old M5.45c's five criteria into the successors once more: (1)->g1 (range parameter deliberately dropped, with the reason and M5.45f named), (2)->g2, (3)->g3, (4)->f1, (5)->h1/h2/h3 plus f(b). Nothing dropped. Verified against source rather than read: M5.62 exists at backlog.md:86 and its 'node-scoped subscriber that NodeSubscriptions owns' is literally the class M5.45h defers to; SPEC.md:53 maps NFR-4 to criterion 9 only and :348/:354 are criteria 8 and 9 as M5.45g describes them; SegmentCacheTest pins both the ceiling (:44) and the exact-N boundary (:147), so M5.45h's precedent claim is real; VERSION_3 exists in SubscriptionEvent; GrantIssuer's javadoc points at SubscriptionHub.deliver (M5.45d), not at a split row, so no stale pointer remains in Java -- grep for M5.45c in *.java returns only the two edited lines. TWO MINORS, both prose inside ADR-0043's Decision (b) section and neither blocking: one paragraph that the repointing walked past still describes the coalescing as a union RANGED GET, and the rewritten Cost paragraph redirects a reader to a note that prices nothing.

findings.title: The repoint at :96-97 handed the paragraph at :101-105 to M5.45h, and that paragraph still describes the coalesced fetch as a union RANGED GET -- which the same record says twice is impossible
findings.summary: ':101-105 -- SO WHAT THE COORDINATES BUY IS COALESCING WITHOUT A DIRECTORY READ ... can union them into ONE ranged GET under ONE key-scoped grant -- which is what "one grant per (node, segment)" means.' The sentence two lines above it now names M5.45h as the owner of that coalescing, so a dead pointer became a live instruction.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.45h's cell cites ADR-0043 by name in its own title ('THE COALESCING ADR-0043 ASSIGNED TO M5.45b BY NAME'), so its taker opens this record. At :96-97 the diff now says the coalescing is 'M5.45h's at the consumer now'; the very next paragraph, untouched, tells them what that coalescing IS: union the K events' byteStart/byteLen into ONE ranged GET. Implementing that is the defect M5.45b round 2 measured -- a union range carries neither the footer nor (for a true [min,max) union) the header, and SegmentReader.open checks the footer magic BEFORE the directory, so every direct delivery throws 'segment is truncated: no footer magic' and ConsumerClient.decodeInto, which opens the whole array with no partial path, never decodes a record. The same record contradicts the paragraph at :62-71 ('The request is a plain GET with no range') and again at :212 ('no range is EXPRESSIBLE, so a whole-object GET'), and M5.45h's own row says 'whole-object GETs' -- so the majority of the tree says the right thing and this is why it is minor rather than major. But it is precisely the shape round 1 raised and this round exists to close: a correction applied to the sentence a finding cited and not to the sentence beside it. Before the diff the paragraph was anchored to M5.39 and M5.45b, both closed or split, so nobody could act on it; naming an open todo row two lines above makes it actionable.
findings.suggested_fix: Either mark the paragraph as conditional on the bounded-read reader M5.45f may or may not authorise ('what the coordinates WOULD buy, if a reader that can decode from a bounded read ever arrives -- see Decision (b)'), or add the same one-clause disclaimer the Status note already carries. Fixing a minor is permitted and usually wrong (review.md rule 11); recording it in the commit body and letting M5.45f's mandated sweep of byteStart/byteLen sites catch it is the cheaper route, since this paragraph is exactly a byteStart/byteLen site and M5.45f criterion 3 requires a per-site disposition IN THIS FILE.

findings.title: The rewritten Cost paragraph sends a reader pricing `direct` to the Status note, and the Status note assigns rows without pricing anything
findings.summary: ':183-186 -- THAT IS NO LONGER THE STATE OF THE TREE ... M5.45d landed ... so a reader pricing `direct` today must read the Status note below rather than this paragraph.' The Status note at :196-220 contains row ownership and dependency ordering and no request count, so the redirect points away from the answer.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone auditing whether serving `direct` costs an object-store request today -- the question this project exists to answer, and the question a Cost heading in an ADR is where you look for -- reads 'must read the Status note below rather than this paragraph', follows it, and finds M5.45f/g/h assignments and an M5.62 dependency. The number they came for is stated nowhere in the record after this edit: the deleted sentence said 'This commit adds no object-store request', and its replacement puts that in the past tense about the original commit while the current state (the hub mints and serves DIRECT, signing is not an object-store request per ADR-0041, and the serving path writes nothing to the sink) is asserted only in SubscriptionHub's comment at :440-444 and in M5.45d's backlog cell. The blast radius is small because the next sentence of the same paragraph does say the consumer-side GET is still issued by nothing -- a careful reader reconstructs it -- but the redirect is false about what it points at, in the one section of this record that carries a cost claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the redirect with the price itself: serving DIRECT adds ZERO object-store requests (signing is not one -- ADR-0041 -- and the sink gets no bytes), and the consumer-side GET those grants authorise will be one whole-object GET per (node, segment) once M5.45h lands, invisible to CountingBinStore. Or drop the pointer and leave the two factual sentences that follow it, which already carry most of the answer.
